summary: Large-file transfer on a bucket you pay cents for: uploads go straight to object storage with presigned URLs, links expire and count downloads, optional passwords, and optional client-side encryption with the key in the URL fragment so the server never sees it.

stack.choice: Cloudflare R2 or Backblaze B2 with presigned URLs
stack.why: files never pass through your server

stack.choice: Web Crypto in the browser, optional

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: An S3-compatible bucket with access keys and CORS
prerequisites.why: Direct browser uploads need CORS on the bucket.
prerequisites.get: R2: create bucket, API token, and set CORS to allow PUT from your domain. B2: similar under bucket settings.
prerequisites.cost: cents to a few dollars a month

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. The page and link table need a small always-on process.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

phases.title: Upload
phases.goal: Presigned PUTs from the browser with progress; multipart over 100 MB; nothing touches your disk.

steps.detail: transfers (id long random slug, created_at, expires_at, downloads, max_downloads, password_hash, note), files (id, transfer_id, key, name, size, content_type). Keys random, never the filename.
commands: mkdir send && cd send && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3@3 @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner@3

steps.do: The upload page with progress and multipart for large files

check: A 2 GB file uploads with progress without touching the server's disk
A transfer over the cap is refused before upload starts

phases.title: Download
phases.goal: A file list, short-lived presigned GETs, counted downloads, a limit.

steps.do: /t/:slug with the list and presigned GET per file with the original filename
Count downloads and refuse after max_downloads

check: The recipient downloads with the original filename

phases.title: Expiry and passwords
phases.goal: Expired links explain themselves; objects are deleted; passwords are rate limited.

steps.do: Default 7-day expiry; nightly job deleting objects and rows
Optional password with constant-time compare and a rate limit

check: An expired link returns a clear page
Objects are gone from the bucket
A wrong password is rate limited

phases.title: Encryption
phases.goal: Key in the fragment; server never sees it.

steps.do: Encrypt in the browser with Web Crypto before upload; key in the URL fragment

check: The recipient's download is the original file

phases.title: Deploy
phases.goal: Lifecycle rules as a backstop, healthz, service, README.

steps.do: README with the cost model and the fragment-key design

check: A stranger receives and downloads a file using only the link

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the transfer page is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: File transfer for a small team on your domain, cheaper and more private than the service it replaces.

operations.backup: SQLite nightly; objects are transient by design.
operations.restore: Copy back; expired objects are gone regardless.
operations.incident: Rotate bucket keys if leaked; presigned URLs are short-lived.

releaseGate: Presigned upload verified without server disk use

notIncluded: Worldwide CDN bandwidth, the brand, email delivery and receipts, the apps.
after: Email the link on request via a provider
Upload from a phone via a share target
